newsitem.title: USA: Texas spot power prices steady to higher with gas.
newsitem.headline: Texas spot power prices steady to higher with gas.

text.p: Spot wholesale electricity prices in the Electric Reliability Council of Texas (ERCOT) were steady to higher Wednesday with upward pressure from higher spot natural gas prices, industry sources said.
Demand for spot power in Texas was said to be relatively thin due to mild weather reaching as high as the low-80s degrees Fahrenheit in south Texas.

Spot gas prices were said to have climbed in the state Wednesday to the $3.30s per million British thermal units on forecasts of cooler weather and expectations of hefty storage withdrawal data from the American Gas Association.
ERCOT firm, peak power for Thursday delivery was pegged at $30.50-32.50 from $29.00-31.00 on Tuesday for Wednesday delivery, the brokers and marketers said.
Non-firm peak ERCOT was discussed higher at $27.00-28.00 from $22.00-23.00 on Tuesday, the sources said.
Firm off-peak ERCOT power transactions were pegged higher at $13.00-15.00 from $11.00-14.00 on Tuesday.
Non-firm off peak ERCOT power was assessed at $11.00-13.00 per MWh.
ERCOT January/February peak power prices were said to have moved higher, with bids at $30.00 from a Tuesday range of $29.75-30.25, the sources said.
Forecasts called for near-normal temperatures through south Texas from December 16 to 19, while north Texas was called to see below normal temperatures during the same period.
